note: Keyed on engine code, not model. The catalogue assigns oil specs by era + fuel + displacement bucket, so every Yaris engine from the 1.0 1KR-FE to the 1.8 2ZR-FE carried one generated value ('5W-30 / A5-B5 / C2 / Asian OEM Standard') and a capacity derived from displacement. Those ACEA C-class requirements are inventions: a 1ZZ-FE or 2ZR-FE asks only for API SL/SM, which is also why the hot-climate alternative was being suppressed on engines that tolerate it perfectly well. Codes listed here also apply to Lexus, Subaru, Mini and Ford models that use the same Toyota engine.

engines.source: motorreviewer.com Toyota 2ZR-FE/FAE/FXE: SAE 5W-20, capacity 4.2 L. Toyota's European manuals list 5W-30 for this engine and the US manual 5W-20/0W-20; 5W-30 is the grade that covers both and suits Tunisian ambient temperatures. No ACEA C-class requirement - the catalogue's C2 was generated, not specified.

motorreviewer.com 2ZR-FXE capacity 4.2 L. Atkinson-cycle hybrid engine (Prius III, Auris HSD, CT200h) specified 0W-20 by Toyota; a heavier grade is not an option here, which is why the hot-climate alternative is withheld.
AMSOIL / OilType factory lookup for Corolla 1.8 1ZZ-FE: 5W-30 all temperatures, API SJ/SL/SM, 4.4 US qt (4.2 L) with filter.

Same ZZ family as the 1ZZ-FE (Corolla E12 1.4/1.6), sharing its 5W-30 API SJ/SL/SM requirement; the smaller-displacement variants take ~3.7 L rather than 4.2 L. Family-derived from the sourced 1ZZ-FE figures, not a model-specific manual.
ZR family shared with the sourced 2ZR-FE (Auris/Corolla E15 1.6 Valvematic), same 4.2 L sump. Family-derived.
2.0 ZR (Avensis T27, RAV4 A3). Family-derived from the sourced 2ZR-FE; the 2.0 takes marginally more than the 1.8.
NZ family (Yaris P1/P9 1.3/1.5, Corolla). Toyota specifies 5W-30 API SL for this generation; ~3.7 L with filter. No ACEA requirement.
Prius II / Yaris Hybrid Atkinson-cycle hybrid. Toyota listed 5W-30 for the Prius II era (0W-20 came with the 2ZR-FXE).
SZ family (Yaris P1 1.0/1.3). Toyota specifies 5W-30 API SJ/SL; no ACEA C-class requirement.
1.0 three-cylinder shared with the Aygo/C1/107. Small sump, ~3.0 L with filter. Later builds are specified 0W-20; 5W-30 covers the range sold in Tunisia.
1.33 Dual VVT-i (Yaris P13, Auris E15). Non-FKE variant, no low-SAPS requirement.
FKE denotes the Atkinson-cycle high-compression variants (Yaris P13 facelift, Yaris Ativ), which Toyota specifies 0W-20 for. A heavier grade is withheld deliberately.
1.2 turbo (Auris E18, C-HR). Turbocharged direct injection specified 0W-20 by Toyota.
Dynamic Force 1.5 (Yaris XP210). Specified 0W-16 with 0W-20 as the permitted alternative; both are thin-oil grades where a heavier oil is not an option.
AZ family (Avensis T25, RAV4 A2/A3, Camry). Toyota specifies 5W-30 API SL; ~4.3 L with filter.
3.0 V6 (Camry, Previa). 5W-30 API SJ/SL, ~4.5 L with filter.
3.4 V6 (4Runner, Land Cruiser Prado 90). 5W-30 API SJ/SL, ~5.4 L.
4.0 V6 (Land Cruiser Prado 120/150, FJ Cruiser, Hilux). 5W-30, ~6.1 L with filter.
4.7 V8 (Land Cruiser 100/200, Lexus LX470). 5W-30, ~6.6 L with filter.
RZ family (Hilux, Hiace, 4Runner 2.4/2.7). 5W-30 API SJ/SL.
A-series (Corolla E9-E11, Carina E). Pre-1998 engines with wider bearing clearances; Toyota's grade tables for these list 10W-30/10W-40 across normal ambient ranges and heavier still above 40 C.
S-series 2.0/2.2 (Carina E, Avensis T22, Celica, RAV4 A1). Same era and grade table as the A-series.

TorqueBot / RoughTrax Hilux specifications: the 2GD-FTV and 1GD-FTV (2015+) take 0W-30 full synthetic meeting Toyota LL-B; 2GD-FTV capacity 5.5 L. DPF-equipped, so the low-SAPS grade is a requirement and no heavier alternative is offered.
TorqueBot / RoughTrax Hilux specifications: 1GD-FTV 2.8 requires 7.0 L of 0W-30 Toyota LL-B.
TorqueBot Hilux oil specifications: 1KD-FTV 3.0 D-4D takes 5W-30 diesel spec, 6.0 L including the 0.5 L filter.

TorqueBot Hilux oil specifications: 2KD-FTV 2.5 D-4D recommended 5W-30 or 5W-40 depending on climate and driving conditions - the heavier grade is exactly the hot-climate case, so the alternative is offered here.
1.4 D-4D (Yaris, Corolla E12, Verso, and the Mini One D and Subaru Trezia that use the same Toyota engine). Particulate-filter equipped in European trim, so a low-SAPS C2 oil is a requirement.
2.0 D-4D (Avensis T22/T25, RAV4 A2, Corolla E12). Pre-DPF, so ACEA B-class rather than low-SAPS C-class.
2.0/2.2 D-4D (Avensis T25/T27, RAV4 A3/A4, Auris, Lexus IS 220d). DPF-equipped, low-SAPS required.
1.6/2.0 D-4D in the Auris E18, Avensis T27 and Verso - BMW N47-derived units supplied to Toyota. DPF-equipped.

PSA-sourced HDi units in the Toyota Proace (badge-engineered Peugeot Expert / Citroen Jumpy). Grade taken from the PSA original (B71 2312 family, low-SAPS C2); capacity is the PSA DW10 figure and is not from a Toyota manual.

Toyota L-family indirect-injection diesels (Hilux, Hiace, Land Cruiser Prado 70/90). These carried no fuel marker in their engine code and were consequently recorded as petrol. Pre-common-rail, pre-DPF: a 15W-40 CD/CF mineral or semi-synthetic is the conventional grade and suits Tunisian ambient temperatures.
Toyota C-family 1.8/2.0/2.2 indirect-injection diesels (Corolla, Carina, Avensis T22, Corona). Also recorded as petrol for want of a marker in the code.
3.0 turbo-diesel (Land Cruiser Prado 90/95, Hilux Surf, 4Runner). Pre-common-rail; 15W-40 is the conventional grade for hot climates.
4.2 six-cylinder diesels (Land Cruiser 70/78/79/80/105). Large sump, ~8 L; 15W-40 CF-4 is the conventional grade.

Toyota B-family diesels (Land Cruiser 70, Dyna, Coaster). Recorded as petrol. Grade is the conventional 15W-40 for pre-common-rail Toyota diesels; the capacity is a family figure, not from a model manual.
